title: ForgeSight checkpoint
raw_text:
ForgeSight checkpoint — 28 August 2026, 10:00
Present: Marcus (Head of Product), Priya (Eng Lead), Dana (Customer Success), Tom (Sales). Wei (Design) sent regrets.

Marcus (Head of Product): Two weeks. Priya, you asked for the first slot.
Priya (Eng Lead): I did, and it's the render budget. We built the spike. On a normal customer workspace we are at one point four seconds, comfortably inside two. On Northwind's largest workspace we are at six and I do not have a route to two that doesn't involve pre-aggregating everything.
Marcus (Head of Product): How close can you get?
Priya (Eng Lead): Four. Four I can hold.
Marcus (Head of Product): Then we move it. The first chart renders in under two seconds on a standard workspace, and under four seconds on Northwind's largest workspace. That is the number now.
Tom (Sales): Four is still better than the eleven we're demoing.
Marcus (Head of Product): Anything else on that?
Priya (Eng Lead): Yes, and this is the uncomfortable one. To get four I need to pre-aggregate, and pre-aggregation does not fit in the warehouse. We are standing up a separate aggregation store alongside it, and there is a nightly pipeline that builds it.
Marcus (Head of Product): You sat in this room a fortnight ago and said no second database, no new pipeline.
Priya (Eng Lead): I did. I was wrong. Either the number goes or the constraint goes, and you have already told the board the number.
Marcus (Head of Product): Fine. Noted, and I want it noted as a reversal, not as something we always intended.
Dana (Customer Success): Can I do the scheduled report, because it has grown since we spoke.
Marcus (Head of Product): Go.
Dana (Customer Success): Two things came back from Halcyon. First, PDF is not enough. Their finance team wants the file in a spreadsheet. So the scheduled report has to go out as a PDF or a CSV, sender's choice. Second, it is never one person. It goes to a distribution list.
Marcus (Head of Product): How many people?
Dana (Customer Success): Halcyon's list is fourteen. Round it up.
Marcus (Head of Product): So a scheduled dashboard report can be sent as a PDF or a CSV, to up to twenty recipients per schedule. That replaces what we wrote down last time.
Dana (Customer Success): And the schedule itself is unchanged, weekly is what everybody picks.
Tom (Sales): New one, and it came out of the Meridian demo on Tuesday. Their ops director filtered a chart, went quiet, and then said, and I wrote it down, "and where do I write what I think this means?" They want to argue about the number inside the tool, not in email.
Marcus (Head of Product): Meaning what, concretely?
Tom (Sales): A user can leave a comment pinned to a specific chart, and everyone with access to that dashboard can see it.
Dana (Customer Success): That is in the ticket queue too, actually. Twice.
Marcus (Head of Product): In. New, and it's in.
Priya (Eng Lead): Scope it small. A comment on a chart, not threads, not mentions, not notifications.
Marcus (Head of Product): Small. Agreed. Right, let's do the round of things that have not moved, so nobody re-litigates them in a fortnight.
Priya (Eng Lead): Every chart must let the user export its underlying rows as CSV. Built, it works.
Marcus (Head of Product): Unchanged.
Priya (Eng Lead): ForgeSight must authenticate users through the customer's own SAML identity provider, and we store no passwords ourselves. Northwind's Okta tenant is wired up in staging.
Marcus (Head of Product): Unchanged.
Priya (Eng Lead): Access is scoped by role, so a regional manager only sees rows for their own region. Enforced in the query. That has not changed and it is not going to.
Marcus (Head of Product): Unchanged. And the date is the date. The pilot has to be in front of Northwind by the thirtieth of November. Nobody has moved that.
Tom (Sales): Nobody has moved that.
Dana (Customer Success): The audit log is still on, isn't it? Meridian will ask again.
Marcus (Head of Product): Still on, still as written, no change.
Marcus (Head of Product): Good. Priya, write up the aggregation store thing properly so it doesn't look like we forgot what we said.
